results.input: Near the end, what did Ragueneau say Moliere had taken from you, and what did you answer?
results.reply:
Ragueneau came in sobbing to say Moliere had stolen a whole scene from me — the one from 'Scapin', "Que Diable allait-il faire?" — played the day before to huge laughter. And I answered him, "Tut! He did well!" then asked how the scene went, whether it told. It told, it seems!

For I saw it plainly: my whole life has been to be the prompter every one forgets — there under your balcony that night, Le Bret, at the foot of the ladder while another climbed to Love and Fame. Moliere mounts; I stay in the shadow. Very just, I said, very just — here at the threshold of death I pay my tribute too, to Moliere's genius and Christian's fair face.
